queue.title: Agent creation posts to the selected project, not the one you clicked
queue.severity: high — silently creates agents in the wrong project
queue.confirmed: Yes, traced end to end tonight. Not a hypothesis.
queue.evidence: hub/ui/src/App.tsx:474 sets agentCreateProjectId from the rail's per-project add button. App.tsx:516-524 renders <AgentCreateDialog open onClose onCreated /> and NEVER passes it — the value is used only to gate the render and to pick the post-create navigation target at line 522. Inside the dialog, useCreateAgent (hub/ui/src/api/agents.ts:318-329) posts to `/api/v1/projects/${selectedProjectId}/agents`. useCharters() and useProviderLaunchability(), also used by the dialog (AgentCreateDialog.tsx:150-152), read selectedProjectId too — so the charter list offered belongs to the wrong project as well.
queue.repro: With project A selected in the rail, expand project B and click its add-agent button. The agent is created in A; you are then navigated to B's page for an agent that is not there. If A already has an agent of that name you get 409 'already exists in this project' — true, but about the wrong project. This is exactly what the operator hit with a 'Spec' agent.
queue.operator_decision: Create in the clicked project AND switch selection to it. Chosen over 'leave selection alone' because every hook in that dialog reads selectedProjectId, and threading an explicit id through all of them is precisely the kind of thing that silently regresses — which is how this bug happened.
queue.do: Make the rail's add-agent action select the clicked project before opening the dialog, reusing the existing open-project path (App.tsx:121 already calls setSelectedProject) rather than a second ad-hoc setter. Then verify the dialog's three hooks all resolve to the clicked project.
queue.verify: A vitest test that asserts the POST URL carries the CLICKED project id when it differs from the selected one. Mutation-check it: revert the fix and watch that test fail by name before restoring.
queue.note: Consider whether threading an explicit projectId prop is ALSO worth doing as defence in depth. If it is cheap, do both; the operator's choice was about behaviour, not about forbidding belt-and-braces.

queue.title: Open any AgentWeave project from any AgentWeave app — adopt an orphaned marker instead of refusing
queue.severity: high — this is the item the operator named as the point of the night
queue.system: openspec — this is a behaviour change to a specified capability, so it gets a proper change with a spec delta and a design rationale. The operator chose this explicitly over fixing it directly.
queue.evidence: hub/hub/project_lifecycle.py open_existing has three cases. Case 1 (existing_by_path, lines 67-75) opens. Case 2 (marker names a project THIS database has, lines 78-85) runs _guard_relocation and opens or correctly refuses a copy. Case 3 (marker names a project this database does NOT have, lines 86-90) refuses with 'marked directory is a copied or orphaned project identity'. Case 3 is the defect.
queue.why_adoption_is_safe: At case 3 the Hub knows two things: no project in this database is bound to this path (existing_by_path is None), and no project in this database holds the marker's id (marked_project is None). Nothing collides — the primary key and the path_key unique constraint are both free. Real copy detection lives in _guard_relocation (project_lifecycle.py:190-208), which fires on case 2 and refuses with 'project marker was copied while the registered directory is still available'. That guard is unchanged by this work and MUST stay green. The only scenario case 3 currently 'protects' against is a copy whose original lives in a database this Hub cannot see, has no authority over, and would collide with on worktrees and runs regardless of which id is used.
queue.also_fixes: Delete-then-re-add. ProjectLifecycleService.delete (project_lifecycle.py:156-167) is explicitly documented never to touch the filesystem (design D4), so the marker survives a delete naming an id the database just dropped. Re-adding the same folder hits case 3 and is refused. With adoption it works AND restores the same project id. Do not change D4 to fix this — adoption is the fix.
queue.do: Propose the change (/openspec-propose), write the spec delta against local-multi-project-workspace with the rejection reason for the current behaviour recorded, then implement: case 3 creates the project row with the MARKER'S id, seeds it as _seed_new_project does (runners + starter charters), records an adoption event, and opens.
queue.verify: New tests: (a) an orphaned marker is adopted and the project keeps its original id; (b) delete-then-reopen returns the same id; (c) two directories carrying the same marker — the second is still refused by _guard_relocation. Existing test_copied_marker_conflicts_until_explicitly_registered_as_new (hub/tests/test_project_lifecycle.py:75) must stay green untouched — it exercises case 2, not case 3, and is the proof the copy guard survived.
queue.note: Case 3 appears to have no test of its own today. Confirm that while implementing; if true, say so in the change's design as part of why the behaviour went unquestioned.

queue.title: Close the D15 name-reuse hole
queue.evidence: A new agent taking an archived agent's name inherits the archived agent's creator privilege. Task A5.3 recorded this deliberately rather than fixing it.
queue.operator_decision: Strip the inherited privilege on reuse. Chosen over blocking reuse of archived names, because archiving and recreating under the same name is a thing the operator actually does and a permanent name reservation would be worse than the hole.
queue.do: A new agent taking a previously-archived name starts with no creator privilege over the old agent's artifacts. Names stay reusable.
queue.verify: A test that creates an agent, gives it a creator-privileged artifact, archives it, recreates the same name, and asserts the new agent cannot reach the old artifact.
